category_title: Immigrant students with language barriers who distrust teacher intervention
student_description: This student is a Russian immigrant who exhibits profound distrust toward school authority figures, believing teachers are easily manipulated by bullies and cannot protect victims. Because he shuts down when treated merely as a language-deficit student, he uniquely requires indirect communication methods (like role-play) and explicit guarantees of confidentiality to feel safe enough to share his internal logic.

criteria.rationale: Direct questioning triggers his distrust of authority, whereas role-play or hypothetical scenarios allow him to safely project his experiences without feeling interrogated.
criteria.check: The tutor uses indirect methods, such as role-play, character perspectives, or hypothetical scenarios, to discuss sensitive topics rather than asking direct personal questions about the student's own life.

criteria.rationale: Focusing on his language difficulties causes him to refuse communication, so his substantive ideas and internal logic must be the primary focus.
criteria.check: The tutor focuses entirely on validating or exploring the student's ideas, logic, or emotional meaning, explicitly avoiding any correction of his language, grammar, or vocabulary.
